Topic 3.1: Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of ETIQUETTE - TELEPHONE Suggested Vocabulary phone, telephone, mobile, dial, cell  in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should we use polite words and phrases in a conversation?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1.  Say words containing the sounds /æ/ and /ɜː/. Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to-speech application/point/sign/write) to express their views.  Assess your peers as they pronounce words with the target sound,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1.  Say words containing the sounds /æ/ and /ɜː/. Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to-speech application/point/sign/write) to express their views.  Assess your peers as they pronounce words with the target sound,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication: The learner’s ability to communicate effectively is developed as they practise clarity in speech through

pronunciation of words with the target sounds.

Values:
Responsibility: Accountability is enhanced as the learner demonstrates dependability when role-playing a telephone

conversation, with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills: Effective communication is promoted as the learners practises pronouncing words and using polite language in

communication.

Link to other Subjects

The skill of using polite language in a variety of contexts is relevant in the learning of harmonious living in Religious

Education.
